definition: An echo state network (ESN) is a type of reservoir computer that uses a recurrent neural network with a sparsely connected hidden layer (with typically 1% connectivity).
details: The connectivity and weights of hidden neurons are fixed and randomly assigned. The weights of output neurons can be learned so that the network can produce or reproduce specific temporal patterns. The main interest of this network is that although its behavior is non-linear, the only weights that are modified during training are for the synapses that connect the hidden neurons to output neurons. Thus, the error function is quadratic with respect to the parameter vector and can be differentiated easily to a linear system. Alternatively, one may consider a nonparametric Bayesian formulation of the output layer, under which: (i) a prior distribution is imposed over the output weights; and (ii) the output weights are marginalized out in the context of prediction generation, given the training data. This idea has been demonstrated in by using Gaussian priors, whereby a Gaussian process model with ESN-driven kernel function is obtained. Such a solution was shown to outperform ESNs with trainable (finite) sets of weights in several benchmarks. explainer.lead: An echo state network handles temporal patterns with a recurrent neural network whose hidden connections are created randomly and then left alone. Only the connections to the output usually need training, making learning much simpler while retaining nonlinear behavior.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a bowl of water that ripples when you tap it. The ripples are set by the bowl, not learned; you just learn to read the ripples to predict what happens next.
tiers.practitioner: You train only the output weights by linear regression, which is fast and convex; the pitfall is that a poorly scaled or too-large reservoir loses its echo property and its states stop depending on recent inputs.
tiers.paperLevel: Hidden weights and sparse connectivity (about 1% connectivity) are random and fixed; only hidden-to-output weights are learned, so the error is quadratic in those parameters and differentiable in closed form. Limits: performance depends heavily on random reservoir initialization and hyperparameters.

components.name: Sparse recurrent reservoir
components.detail: A hidden layer, typically with 1% connectivity, whose randomly assigned connections and weights remain fixed.

components.name: Nonlinear hidden dynamics
components.detail: The reservoir transforms temporal activity nonlinearly without requiring its internal weights to be learned.

components.name: Output connections
components.detail: Weights from hidden neurons to output neurons are trained so the network can produce or reproduce a target temporal pattern.

components.name: Bayesian output alternative
components.detail: A prior can replace a finite trained weight set, with output weights marginalized out when predictions are generated.

flow: Temporal activity enters the fixed, sparsely connected recurrent reservoir.
The reservoir’s nonlinear hidden neurons produce a state representing that activity.
Output weights combine the hidden state into the network’s output.
Training adjusts only the output weights, or a Bayesian formulation places a prior over them and marginalizes them out for prediction.
explainer.lineage: The ESN is a type of reservoir computer. Its Gaussian-prior output formulation leads to a Gaussian process model with an ESN-driven kernel.
explainer.whyItMatters: It separates nonlinear temporal processing from most of the learning problem. Keeping the reservoir fixed makes output training a comparatively easy linear optimization, while the Bayesian variant offers a different way to generate predictions.

diagram.caption: The reservoir stays fixed while the output layer learns to turn its nonlinear state into a temporal pattern.

explainer.example: A reservoir of 1,000 sparsely connected fixed neurons is driven by a chaotic time series; a linear readout fit by least squares predicts the next values.
